8e80175cb306.Virtual appliance: A virtual appliance next hop sends traffic to a network virtual appliance (NVA) such as a firewall VM for inspection, not straight out to the internet as this question requires.
8e80175cb306.Virtual network: The Virtual network next hop keeps traffic inside the virtual network address space; it cannot be used to send matching traffic directly to the internet.
8e80175cb306.Virtual network gateway: A virtual network gateway next hop sends traffic to a VPN or ExpressRoute gateway, typically toward on-premises networks, rather than directly out to the internet.

130418afdf41.Because IP forwarding enables accelerate: Accelerated networking is a separate network interface setting based on SR-IOV. IP forwarding only lets the interface accept and send packets not addressed to its own IP.
130418afdf41.Because IP forwarding lets the VM's NIC: IP forwarding does not advertise or create routes. You still add a user-defined route with a Virtual appliance next hop, and BGP exchange needs a gateway or Azure Route Server.
130418afdf41.Because IP forwarding disables the defau: IP forwarding does not change network security group rules, which still apply to the interface. It only allows the VM to receive and forward traffic for other destinations.

3ab04b370c17.Virtual appliance: A Virtual appliance next hop sends traffic to the private IP of a network virtual appliance, not to the VPN gateway that connects to on-premises.
3ab04b370c17.Virtual network: The Virtual network next hop keeps traffic within the virtual network's address space, so it cannot send traffic through the VPN gateway to on-premises.
3ab04b370c17.Virtual network service endpoint: Virtual network service endpoint is a system next hop that Azure adds for service endpoints. You cannot choose it as the next hop of a user-defined route.

49decaca346b.It extends routing to peered virtual net: The Virtual network next hop keeps traffic within the local virtual network's address space. Traffic to peered networks uses the system routes that peering creates.
49decaca346b.It applies to inbound traffic entering t: Route tables control how outbound traffic leaving a subnet is routed. Filtering which sources can reach resources is the job of network security groups.
49decaca346b.It is advertised to on-premises networks: User-defined routes are not advertised over BGP to on-premises networks. They only affect routing for the subnets the route table is associated with.

218caecd303e.To distribute incoming connections evenl: Spreading connections across a backend pool is what Azure Load Balancer does. User-defined routes change the next hop for traffic, they do not balance load.
218caecd303e.To connect two virtual networks privatel: Private connectivity between virtual networks without a gateway is provided by virtual network peering, not by user-defined routes.
218caecd303e.To filter inbound and outbound traffic b: Filtering traffic by port and protocol is done with network security groups. Route tables decide where traffic goes, not whether it is allowed.

f034063537d6.Budgets can only be scoped to subscripti: The portal supports budgets at several scopes, including management groups, resource groups, and billing scopes, not just subscriptions.
f034063537d6.Budgets reset automatically on a weekly: Budget reset periods are monthly, quarterly, annually, or billing month, quarter, or year. There is no weekly reset period.
f034063537d6.Budgets can only alert on forecasted cos: Budgets support both actual cost and forecasted cost thresholds, so they are not limited to forecasted costs.

dd9f1bfb15a1.Azure deallocates the virtual machines i: Budgets do not affect resources. Microsoft Learn states that resources aren't affected and consumption isn't stopped when a threshold is exceeded.
dd9f1bfb15a1.Azure applies a spending limit to the su: A budget does not set a spending limit or block deployments. It only sends notifications, optionally calling an action group you configure.
dd9f1bfb15a1.Azure raises a Service Health alert for: Service Health alerts report Azure service issues and maintenance. Budget thresholds trigger budget alert emails to the recipients set on the budget.

9a66a7d67483.Enterprise Agreement enrollments only, s: Microsoft Customer Agreement billing accounts, billing profiles, and invoice sections all support budgets, so budget alerts are not limited to Enterprise Agreement.
9a66a7d67483.Pay-as-you-go subscriptions only, becaus: Enterprise Agreement and Microsoft Customer Agreement accounts support budget alerts too. Department spending quota alerts are an additional EA feature, not a replacement.
9a66a7d67483.Microsoft Customer Agreement accounts on: Enterprise Agreement accounts support budget alerts as well. Credit alerts are an extra EA alert type for Azure Prepayment, not a replacement for budgets.

55dc7335b834.Only on the Budgets page in the Azure po: In the Azure portal, budgets are defined by cost. Usage-based budgets are defined through the Azure Consumption API instead.
55dc7335b834.Only by configuring an Azure Monitor met: Azure Monitor metric alerts watch resource metrics, not budget consumption. Usage-based budgets are defined through the Azure Consumption API.
55dc7335b834.Only through a Cost Management export to: Exports write cost data to storage on a schedule and do not create or send budget alerts. Usage-based budgets need the Azure Consumption API.

5eba611dc83e.Budget alerts: Budget alerts are a supported Cost Management alert type that fires when spending reaches a budget threshold, so this is not the unsupported option the question is looking for.
5eba611dc83e.Credit alerts: Credit alerts are a supported Cost Management alert type that notifies you when Azure Prepayment credits are being consumed, so they are not the unsupported option.
5eba611dc83e.Department spending quota alerts: Department spending quota alerts are supported for Enterprise Agreement departments when spending reaches a quota threshold, so they are a real Cost Management alert type.

519b18fe20b7.No, recipients must be tenant users with: Budget alert recipients are plain email addresses. They do not need to be tenant users or hold any Cost Management role.
519b18fe20b7.No, external addresses must first be inv: You do not need to invite recipients as guest users. You can type any email address, including addresses outside your organization.
519b18fe20b7.Yes, but external recipients must be rea: External addresses can be added directly as email recipients of the budget. An action group is optional and not required for external recipients.

ecfaba106b47.Budget alerts enforce a hard spending ca: Budget alerts do not enforce a cap. Microsoft Learn states that resources aren't affected and consumption isn't stopped when thresholds are exceeded.
ecfaba106b47.Budget alerts are evaluated in real time: Cost data typically arrives within 8 to 24 hours and budgets are evaluated every 24 hours, so alerts are not real time.
ecfaba106b47.Budget alerts are scoped to a single res: Budgets can be created at management group, subscription, and resource group scopes, as well as EA and MCA billing scopes.

58919e30200d.Credit alert for Azure Prepayment: Credit alerts fire at 90% and 100% of the Azure Prepayment balance. They do not track a department's spending against its assigned quota.
58919e30200d.Cost anomaly alert for the department: Anomaly alerts flag unusual spending patterns detected for a subscription. They do not measure a department's spend against its EA quota.
58919e30200d.Reservation utilization alert: Reservation utilization alerts warn when reserved capacity is underused. They have nothing to do with department spending quotas.

f1d02de66648.Resource locks: Resource locks prevent accidental deletion or modification. They protect resources rather than adding descriptive metadata for organizing them.
f1d02de66648.Role assignments: Role assignments grant access permissions through Azure role-based access control. They control who can do what, not how resources are categorized.
f1d02de66648.Azure Policy definitions: Policy definitions describe rules that resources must comply with. They can require or add tags, but the metadata itself is the tag.

ecc15b204fe3.Tag names are case‑sensitive, while tag: This reverses the documented behavior. Tag names are case-insensitive for operations, while tag values are case-sensitive.
ecc15b204fe3.Tag names and tag values are both case‑s: Tag names are case-insensitive for operations, so a tag is retrieved or updated regardless of the name's casing. Only values are case-sensitive.
ecc15b204fe3.Tag names and tag values are both case‑i: Tag values are case-sensitive, so 'Prod' and 'prod' are different values. Only tag names are case-insensitive.

acd30c5db4d1.Resource group: Resource groups support tags, so this is not a place where tags are unavailable. Management groups are the scope that does not support tags.
acd30c5db4d1.Subscription: Microsoft Learn states you can apply tags to resources, resource groups, and subscriptions, so subscriptions do support tags.
acd30c5db4d1.Public IP address: A public IP address is an ordinary Azure resource and supports tags like other resources.

52f49e08d93d.Store cost center identifiers in resourc: Cost analysis can group and filter by tags directly, and names cannot be changed later. Tags are the recommended way to carry cost allocation data.
52f49e08d93d.Combine all cost allocation details into: Separate, consistent tag keys are easier to filter and group in cost reports. A combined value is hard to query and tag values are limited to 256 characters.
52f49e08d93d.Apply tags once at deployment and avoid: Changing tags does not break cost reporting. Cost data reflects the tags present when usage occurred, and keeping tags current is part of good practice.

ae872a51bbda.Contributor: Contributor can apply tags but also lets you create, modify, and delete resources, which is broader than tag management requires.
ae872a51bbda.Resource Policy Contributor: Resource Policy Contributor manages Azure Policy definitions and assignments. It does not grant write access to the tags resource type.
ae872a51bbda.Cost Management Contributor: Cost Management Contributor manages budgets, exports, and cost views. It does not grant permission to write tags on resources.

2197efa5a277.Yes, tags set on a resource group are co: Resources don't inherit tags applied to a resource group or subscription, whether they are created before or after the tag is set.
2197efa5a277.Yes, enabling tag inheritance in Cost Ma: Cost Management tag inheritance applies tags to cost and usage records for reporting. It does not write tags onto the resources themselves.
2197efa5a277.No, and Azure Policy cannot add tags to: Azure Policy can add or replace tags on existing resources by using the Modify effect with a remediation task.

dc3c5985759c.Because tag values are limited to 256 ch: The 256-character limit is real, but it is not the reason. Tag values are stored in plain text and readable by anyone with read access.
dc3c5985759c.Because Azure Policy automatically remov: There is no built-in policy that scans and removes secret-like tag values. The concern is that tag values are visible in plain text.
dc3c5985759c.Because tags are encrypted with Microsof: Encryption keys are not the issue. Tag values can be read in plain text by any user with read access to the resource.

19a001a04fac.A resource can belong to several resourc: A resource cannot be a member of more than one resource group. Each resource belongs to exactly one.
19a001a04fac.A resource must be in the same region as: Resources in a resource group can be in different regions from the group. The group's location only stores its metadata.
19a001a04fac.A resource group can hold resources from: A resource group exists in one subscription and can only contain resources from that subscription.

8422b2f633ec.All resources must be deployed to the sa: Resources can be in regions different from the resource group, and moving resources between groups does not change their region.
8422b2f633ec.Resources can be in different regions, a: A resource group's location cannot be changed after creation. You would need to create a new group and move the resources.
8422b2f633ec.The resource group location matters for: Each resource is billed at the price for the region it is deployed in. The group's location stores metadata and does not set pricing.

f537afc8de8d.They are moved to a default resource gro: There is no default resource group that collects resources. Deleting a resource group deletes every resource in it.
f537afc8de8d.They remain but become read-only until r: Resources do not survive in a read-only state. Deleting the group deletes the resources it contains.
f537afc8de8d.They keep running until you delete each: You do not have to delete resources one by one. Deleting the resource group deletes all of its resources.

6eb920069b7e.Group resources by resource type, such a: Grouping by resource type splits up resources that are deployed, updated, and deleted together. Guidance is to group resources that share a lifecycle.
6eb920069b7e.Group resources by Azure region so that: Region is not the recommended grouping basis, and a group can hold resources from many regions. Group by shared lifecycle and management needs.
6eb920069b7e.Place resources with different life cycl: Mixing lifecycles means deleting the group removes resources that should outlive others. Resources in a group should share the same lifecycle.

806056a6dddd.Resources can be moved between resource: Many resource types can be moved directly to a resource group in another subscription without redeployment, subject to per-type limitations.
Moving a resource to another resource group does not change its region. Region moves use Azure Resource Mover or redeployment.
During a move, both the source and target resource groups are locked, blocking create, update, and delete operations until the move completes.

e33ad0716755.980 instances, with some exceptions for: 980 is the maximum number of resource groups per subscription, not the number of instances of a resource type in a resource group.
e33ad0716755.250 instances, matching the default stor: 250 is the default number of storage accounts per region per subscription. The per resource group limit for a resource type is 800.
e33ad0716755.50 instances, the same as the tag limit: 50 is the maximum number of tag name-value pairs on a resource. A resource group allows 800 instances of a resource type.

a5a2bb09a89b.It determines the region where every res: Resources in a resource group can be in other regions. The group location does not restrict where its resources are deployed.
a5a2bb09a89b.It determines which region's pricing app: Each resource is billed by the region it is deployed in. The resource group location only governs where its metadata is stored.
a5a2bb09a89b.It determines the paired region that Azu: The resource group location does not configure replication. Resource-level settings such as geo-redundant storage control replication to a paired region.

4e1608c5be36.Azure Resource Manager queues both opera: Concurrent conflicting operations are not both guaranteed to succeed. One proceeds and the other is rejected with a conflict and must be retried.
4e1608c5be36.Azure Resource Manager merges the two re: Resource Manager does not merge separate requests into one operation. Each request is handled on its own, and conflicts are rejected.
4e1608c5be36.Azure Resource Manager rejects both oper: HTTP 429 indicates request throttling, not a concurrency conflict. A conflicting concurrent operation returns 409.

12bdc36af4fc.Availability sets: Availability sets spread VMs across fault and update domains but do not add or remove VM instances automatically based on load.
12bdc36af4fc.Azure Dedicated Host groups: Dedicated hosts provide physical servers reserved for your VMs. They do not automatically scale the number of VM instances.
12bdc36af4fc.Proximity placement groups: Proximity placement groups keep VMs physically close for low latency. They provide no autoscaling or high availability.

f49135985427.Up to 600 instances: 600 is the limit for a scale set created from a managed image. Flexible orchestration supports up to 1,000 instances.
f49135985427.Up to 100 instances: 100 instances is the limit for a Uniform scale set restricted to a single placement group, not the Flexible orchestration limit.
f49135985427.Up to 200 instances: 200 is the maximum number of VMs in an availability set, not the instance limit for a Flexible scale set.

4692d6ea9c28.Automatic scaling based on demand: Automatic scaling based on demand is a core scale set benefit, using autoscale rules or schedules, so it is not the option that fails to describe a benefit.
4692d6ea9c28.Health monitoring and automatic replacem: Scale sets do offer health monitoring and automatic instance repair to replace unhealthy VMs, so this is a genuine benefit rather than the answer.
4692d6ea9c28.Ability to deploy workloads across fault: Scale sets spread instances across fault domains and update domains, or across availability zones, to improve resilience, so this is a real benefit.

98e421c489db.A grouping of VMs that Azure reboots tog: That describes an update domain. A fault domain groups hardware that shares power and networking to limit the impact of hardware failures.
98e421c489db.A physically separate datacenter locatio: That describes an availability zone, which is a larger unit than a fault domain. A fault domain is a hardware grouping such as a rack.
98e421c489db.A logical placement grouping that keeps: That describes a proximity placement group, which aims for low latency. Fault domains spread VMs apart to avoid shared hardware failures.

3c6dac6a086c.A group of VMs that share a common power: That describes a fault domain. Update domains group VMs for planned maintenance so they are rebooted one group at a time.
3c6dac6a086c.A group of VMs in a scale set that recei: That describes automatic OS image upgrades, a scale set feature. An update domain is about which VMs are updated or rebooted together.
3c6dac6a086c.A set of VMs placed in separate datacent: That describes availability zones. Update domains are logical groups for planned maintenance within the infrastructure, not separate datacenters.

b9edf66985de.Uniform mode lets you mix Spot and stand: This reverses the modes. Uniform uses one VM model for identical instances, while Flexible allows mixing sizes and Spot with standard VMs.
b9edf66985de.Flexible mode supports up to 1,000 insta: Uniform scale sets also support up to 1,000 instances when not restricted to a single placement group. The key difference is instance uniformity.
b9edf66985de.Uniform mode spreads instances across av: Both modes support availability zones, and Flexible mode spreads instances across fault domains. This is not the difference between them.

9d1286c116cc.Azure selects zones automatically after: You choose the zones when you create a zonal or zone-spanning scale set. Azure then balances instances across the zones you selected.
9d1286c116cc.Each instance is placed in the zone of t: Resource groups have a region, not an availability zone. Zones for scale set instances are set on the scale set itself.
9d1286c116cc.The zones are inherited from the virtual: Virtual networks and subnets span all zones in a region. They do not determine which zones scale set instances are placed in.

72351c8f5fba.Integration with Azure Load Balancer or: Scale sets integrate with Azure Load Balancer and Application Gateway to distribute traffic across instances, so this is a real capability rather than the answer.
72351c8f5fba.Support for spot virtual machines: Scale sets support Azure Spot Virtual Machines for discounted, interruptible capacity, so this is a genuine capability and not the answer.
72351c8f5fba.Support for auto‑healing and health prob: Scale sets support health probes and automatic instance repair to replace unhealthy VMs, so this is a real capability, not the answer.

67b45ae51f82.You are charged a per-instance managemen: There is no extra charge for the scale set itself. You pay only for the underlying VMs, disks, and networking resources.
67b45ae51f82.You are charged for the maximum instance: Billing follows the instances that actually run. The autoscale maximum is a limit, not a billing quantity.
67b45ae51f82.You are charged only for running instanc: Managed disks keep incurring storage charges even when their VM instances are deallocated, so disks are not free.

c610e880e688.A logical grouping of hardware within a: That describes a fault domain, which is a much smaller unit than an availability zone.
c610e880e688.A pair of regions in the same geography: That describes a region pair. Availability zones are separate datacenter groups inside a single region.
c610e880e688.A set of geographically distributed edge: That describes edge points of presence used by Azure Front Door. Availability zones are datacenter groups within a region.

546392121145.Two zones: Two zones is not the standard. Regions that support availability zones have a minimum of three.
546392121145.Four zones: Four zones is not the typical count. Zone-enabled regions normally have three availability zones.
546392121145.Five zones: Five zones is not typical. Azure regions that support availability zones normally have three.

4beb2451df04.<5 milliseconds: Azure designs inter-zone round-trip latency to be under approximately 2 milliseconds, lower than this figure.
4beb2451df04.<10 milliseconds: Ten milliseconds is far above the design target. Zones in a region are connected with round-trip latency under about 2 milliseconds.
4beb2451df04.<100 microseconds: This is lower than what Azure targets. Zones are kilometers apart and the documented target is under about 2 milliseconds.

a96b7c04ddc7.Zonal deployments: Zonal deployments pin a resource to one specific zone, so they do not replicate across zones or fail over automatically.
a96b7c04ddc7.Geo‑redundant deployments: Geo-redundant deployments replicate data to a secondary region, not across availability zones within the same region.
a96b7c04ddc7.Non‑zonal (regional) deployments: Non-zonal deployments do not specify a zone and give no guaranteed replication or automatic failover between zones.

fe8fc04b1120.Zone‑redundant deployment: Zone-redundant deployments spread or replicate a resource across multiple zones rather than pinning it to one specific zone.
fe8fc04b1120.Non‑zonal (regional) deployment: A non-zonal deployment lets Azure place the resource anywhere in the region without a zone guarantee, so it is not pinned.
fe8fc04b1120.Geo‑redundant deployment: Geo-redundant deployments replicate data to a secondary region. They do not pin a resource to a specific zone.

e791ab13019f.They deploy resources across all zones i: Automatic distribution across zones describes zone-redundant deployments. Non-zonal deployments specify no zone and get no zone resilience.
e791ab13019f.They pin each resource to zone 1 by defa: Non-zonal resources are not pinned to zone 1 or any zone. Azure may place them anywhere in the region.
e791ab13019f.They deploy resources to the paired regi: Non-zonal deployment says nothing about paired regions. Cross-region replication is a separate, service-specific configuration.

39383065f805.Zone mapping is fixed per region, so zon: Logical zones are mapped to physical zones independently for each subscription, so zone 1 can differ between subscriptions.
39383065f805.Zone mapping can vary between resource g: The mapping is set per subscription, not per resource group. All resource groups in a subscription share the same zone mapping.
39383065f805.Zone mapping is assigned per virtual mac: Within one subscription, logical zone 1 always maps to the same physical zone, so VMs in zone 1 share a physical zone.

09b148c7e3f5.Place each application tier in its own s: If any tier sits in one zone, losing that zone breaks the whole application. Each tier should be spread across zones.
09b148c7e3f5.Deploy all tiers to one zone and use a p: A proximity placement group reduces latency but keeps everything in one zone, which is a single point of failure.
09b148c7e3f5.Deploy every tier as non-zonal resources: Azure does not automatically move non-zonal resources to a healthy zone. They may be lost during a zone outage.

8ce9878d9420.Yes, data transfer between availability: Microsoft does not charge for data transfer between availability zones in the same region, unlike global VNet peering.
8ce9878d9420.No, inter-zone transfer is free, but dat: Traffic between subnets in the same virtual network is not billed as data transfer, so the second part of this statement is wrong.
8ce9878d9420.Yes, but the charge is waived when both: There is no inter-zone charge to waive. Data transfer between zones in a region is free regardless of network or resource group.

a8abb00e6bc5.Azure Load Balancer: Azure Load Balancer works at layer 4 on TCP and UDP and cannot inspect URL paths or host headers.
a8abb00e6bc5.Traffic Manager: Traffic Manager is a DNS-based router that never inspects HTTP requests, so it cannot route on URL path or host header.
a8abb00e6bc5.Gateway Load Balancer: Gateway Load Balancer chains network virtual appliances at layer 4. It does not route HTTP requests by URL path or host header.

c8ba4fc44eb6.Azure Load Balancer distributes web traf: This reverses the layers. Azure Load Balancer works at layer 4, while Application Gateway works at layer 7.
c8ba4fc44eb6.Azure Load Balancer routes traffic globa: DNS-based global routing is what Traffic Manager does. Azure Load Balancer forwards TCP and UDP flows rather than answering DNS queries.
c8ba4fc44eb6.Azure Load Balancer terminates TLS and s: This reverses the features. TLS termination and cookie-based affinity are Application Gateway features, while Load Balancer passes traffic through.

c107729b0a65.Standard Load Balancer with NSGs: Network security groups filter by IP, port, and protocol. Neither they nor the layer 4 load balancer inspect HTTP for web attacks.
c107729b0a65.Traffic Manager with endpoint monitoring: Endpoint monitoring only checks endpoint health for DNS routing decisions. Traffic Manager never sees HTTP requests and has no WAF.
c107729b0a65.Azure Firewall Premium with IDPS: Azure Firewall is a network firewall, not a load-balancing service, and its IDPS is not the Web Application Firewall offered with Application Gateway.

f699a2bfa11b.Azure Load Balancer: Azure Load Balancer works at layer 4 and cannot see HTTP URL paths, so it cannot send /images and /video to different backends.
f699a2bfa11b.Traffic Manager: Traffic Manager is DNS-based and chooses an endpoint at name resolution time. It never sees the URL path.
f699a2bfa11b.Gateway Load Balancer: Gateway Load Balancer inserts network virtual appliances into the traffic path at layer 4. It has no URL path-based routing.

68ad7e66ae63.Azure Load Balancer: Azure Load Balancer is a layer 4 pass-through service, so it cannot terminate TLS or issue affinity cookies.
68ad7e66ae63.Traffic Manager: Traffic Manager works only at the DNS level and never handles the client connection, so it cannot terminate SSL or set cookies.
68ad7e66ae63.Gateway Load Balancer: Gateway Load Balancer forwards layer 4 traffic to network virtual appliances. It offers neither SSL termination nor cookie-based affinity.

a7d0dee44fc2.It acts as a reverse proxy at Microsoft: That describes Azure Front Door. Traffic Manager does not proxy traffic. Clients connect directly to the endpoint returned by DNS.
a7d0dee44fc2.It distributes TCP/UDP flows across regi: That describes the cross-region (global) tier of Azure Load Balancer. Traffic Manager uses DNS responses, not an anycast IP.
a7d0dee44fc2.It routes client requests to backends ba: Path routing and caching are layer 7 features of Front Door. Traffic Manager never sees HTTP requests.

84d937f1c110.Application Gateway: Application Gateway is a regional layer 7 load balancer, so it does not route users to the best global endpoint across regions.
84d937f1c110.Azure NAT Gateway: NAT Gateway provides outbound internet connectivity for subnets. It does not route inbound user traffic to endpoints.
84d937f1c110.Gateway Load Balancer: Gateway Load Balancer chains network virtual appliances inside a region. It does not pick global endpoints by performance or location.

daa6872a6927.Azure Traffic Manager: Traffic Manager points clients to endpoints using DNS and does not proxy traffic, so it offers no acceleration, caching, or edge DDoS protection.
daa6872a6927.Application Gateway v2: Application Gateway is a regional layer 7 load balancer, not a global edge entry point with caching and acceleration.
daa6872a6927.Cross-region Load Balancer: The cross-region Load Balancer is a global layer 4 service. It has no HTTP caching, acceleration, or layer 7 routing.

ab99cfccbb12.Distributing RDP and SSH connections acr: Inbound NAT rules for RDP and SSH are an Azure Load Balancer feature. Application Gateway handles only HTTP, HTTPS, and related web traffic.
ab99cfccbb12.Load balancing UDP-based game server tra: UDP traffic needs Azure Load Balancer at layer 4. Application Gateway cannot balance UDP traffic.
ab99cfccbb12.Providing outbound SNAT for VMs without: Outbound SNAT and generic TCP balancing are Load Balancer features. Application Gateway does not provide outbound connectivity for VMs.

520d235465b7.It distributes HTTP requests across back: Routing on URL path and host header is a layer 7 feature of Application Gateway. Azure Load Balancer works at layer 4.
520d235465b7.It terminates TLS connections and re-enc: Azure Load Balancer does not decrypt traffic. TLS termination and re-encryption are Application Gateway or Front Door features.
520d235465b7.It directs clients to backend instances: Returning DNS responses based on endpoint health describes Traffic Manager. Load Balancer forwards the actual TCP and UDP flows.

093cf3883dd9.It supports backend VMs in an availabili: Availability sets spread VMs across fault and update domains within a datacenter, not across availability zones.
093cf3883dd9.It automatically replicates its configur: Standard Load Balancer is a regional resource and does not replicate to a paired region. Multi-region needs the cross-region tier or other services.
093cf3883dd9.It supports path-based routing rules tha: Path-based routing is a layer 7 feature of Application Gateway. Standard Load Balancer works at layer 4.

72e51e5cf22a.A Network Watcher test that measures lat: That describes Network Watcher connection monitor. A health probe checks whether each backend instance can receive traffic.
72e51e5cf22a.A diagnostic setting that streams load b: Diagnostic settings route logs and metrics to destinations. A health probe is the load balancer's own check that decides traffic distribution.
72e51e5cf22a.An agent extension installed on each VM: That describes the Application Health extension for scale sets. Load balancer health probes need no agent and only steer traffic.

6238b8ae035e.Internal Load Balancer: An internal load balancer has only a private frontend IP, so it cannot take traffic from the internet to individual VMs.
6238b8ae035e.Gateway Load Balancer: Gateway Load Balancer chains network virtual appliances to another load balancer's frontend. It does not offer NAT rules to individual VMs.
6238b8ae035e.Azure NAT Gateway: NAT Gateway only provides outbound connectivity for a subnet. It cannot direct inbound internet traffic to individual VMs.

19be146abe10.Standard Load Balancer is free of charge: This reverses the pricing. Standard Load Balancer is billed by rules and data processed, and Basic was offered at no charge.
19be146abe10.Standard Load Balancer is open to inboun: Standard Load Balancer is secure by default and closed to inbound traffic unless a network security group allows it.
19be146abe10.Standard Load Balancer supports layer 7: Both SKUs work at layer 4. URL path routing and TLS offload belong to Application Gateway, not either Load Balancer SKU.

b0aa77ce40b3.It uses destination network address tran: Outbound connections use source NAT to the load balancer's frontend IP. DNAT applies to inbound traffic, and no per-NIC public IP is needed.
b0aa77ce40b3.It proxies each outbound connection thro: Load Balancer does not use Azure Firewall for outbound traffic. It performs SNAT itself through outbound or load balancing rules.
b0aa77ce40b3.It assigns an ephemeral public IP addres: That resembles default outbound access, not Load Balancer. With Load Balancer, VMs share the frontend public IP through SNAT.

b88f2f32921f.Application Gateway: Application Gateway is a regional service, so it cannot route traffic across multiple regions with failover between them.
b88f2f32921f.Azure NAT Gateway: NAT Gateway provides outbound internet access for a subnet. It does not route inbound traffic or fail over between regions.
b88f2f32921f.Internal Load Balancer: An internal load balancer distributes private traffic within one virtual network in one region, with no cross-region failover.

281d5a78cf0a.To route non-HTTP protocols such as TCP: DNS-based routing for any protocol is what Traffic Manager already provides. Front Door handles HTTP and HTTPS only.
281d5a78cf0a.To use the priority, weighted, and geogr: Traffic Manager does offer priority, weighted, and geographic routing methods, so this is not a reason to choose Front Door.
